### Amendment 4: Add Material Adverse Change Clause
**Proposed New Clause 4.6:**
"**4.6 Material Adverse Change**
4.6.1 The Buyer shall have the right to terminate this Agreement by written notice to the Seller at any time prior to Closing if a Material Adverse Change occurs in relation to the Company.
4.6.2 'Material Adverse Change' means any event, circumstance, change or effect that, individually or in the aggregate, has a material adverse effect on the business, assets, financial condition, results of operations or prospects of the Company, taken as a whole.
4.6.3 The following shall not constitute a Material Adverse Change:
(a) changes in general economic, financial or market conditions;
(b) changes affecting the industry in which the Company operates generally;
(c) changes in law or accounting standards;
(d) the announcement or pendency of this Agreement;
(e) any action taken at the written request of the Buyer; or
(f) any matter disclosed in the Disclosure Letter,
provided that, in the case of (a), (b) or (c), such change does not have a disproportionate effect on the Company relative to other participants in the industry in which the Company operates."

- **Narrow Interpretation:** "taken as a whole" - requires holistic assessment, not isolated issues

| Industry-wide changes | Included | Standard | Protects Seller from sector trends | **Add "disproportionate effect" exception** |

**Proposed New Clause 8:**
"**8. WARRANTIES**
8.1 The Seller warrants to the Buyer that each of the warranties set out in Schedule D is true and accurate in all respects as at the date of this Agreement and will be true and accurate in all respects as at the Closing Date.
8.2 The warranties shall survive Closing for a period of 7 years from the Closing Date in respect of tax warranties and 3 years from the Closing Date in respect of all other warranties.

(b) a tipping basket mechanism whereby the Seller shall only be liable for losses exceeding the Deductible, and then for the full amount of such losses; and
(c) an overall cap equal to 50% of the Purchase Price (the "Cap")."

| Large Claim | $10,000,000 | $500,000 | $9,500,000 | Full excess payable |

**Rationale:** Provides essential contractual protection against pre-closing liabilities with market-aligned deductible but requires cap reduction negotiation.

**Current Wording (Clause 12.1):**
